correctness.rationale: The complete finite complex is reconstructed from the explicit Heawood incidence graph. Exhaustive enumeration gives 447859 nonempty faces. Successive element toggles produce 223925 disjoint pairs and, by the repeated-element-matching theorem, an acyclic matching with critical cells only in dimensions 0, 9, and 10, in counts 1, 1, and 7. Exact signed Morse elimination gives the row (1,1,0,0,0,-1,1), which is primitive. Since maps S^9 to S^9 are classified by degree, a unimodular basis change reduces the attaching vector to a single degree-one map, leaving a wedge of six 10-spheres. The face-vector Euler characteristic is 7, agreeing with reduced Euler characteristic 6.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is a canonical cubic symmetric incidence graph and the two-matching complex is a natural higher bounded-degree invariant. Exact higher-matching homotopy types are available for comparatively few graph families; this computation supplies a natural non-complete-bipartite benchmark and a nontrivial primitive Morse cancellation leading to six 10-spheres.
